simple.meaning: פִּיד (pîyd) is a Hebrew word meaning “(figuratively) misfortune.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּיד (H6365) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 30:24, with occurrences in Job, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּיד (H6365) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּיד (H6365) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּיד (pîyd) / H6365 is traced through Job 30:24, Job 31:29, Proverbs 24:22 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6365. pid מִּיד noun [masculine] ruin, disaster ; — absolute Job 12:5 ; construct 31:29 ; Prov 24:22 ; suffix מִּידוֺ Job 30:24 + 21:20 (for כִּיד ). מֵּיוֺת מִּיּוֺת, see מֶּה . מִּיחַ see פוח .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root probably meaning to pierce ;

occurrences.englishText: “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall?
“If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me,
for their calamity will rise suddenly.
